problem:
$$
A=[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 & 6 \\ 0 & 6 & 6 \\ -2 & -1 & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

The matrix above has eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=4,$ ${\lambda }_{2}=3,$ and ${\lambda }_{3}=0.$ Find a Jordan canonical form of the matrix.
worked_solution:
Notice that we are given a $3\times 3$ matrix that has precisely $3$ distinct eigenvalues. 

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, and its Jordan canonical form is

$$
{J}_{1}(4)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(3)\,⊕\,{J}_{1}(0)=[\begin{aligned}4 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 3 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

**Note:** The Jordan canonical form is unique up to the order of the Jordan blocks.
